header:
Date: 2027-08-19
Time: 15:00 PT (60 min scheduled)
Actual duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Praesidio CTO), Leah Wong (Head of Cloud Ops), Ravi Shah (Security Lead), Erin Cole (Product)
Recording ID: ff-2027-08-19-praesidio-001
summary: POC scoping to align on endpoint isolation approach (PrivateLink vs VPC peering), success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput, cost targets), workload sizing, benchmark plan, and timeline. Customer is a regulated financial services firm with strict egress/region constraints and internal KMS requirements.
topics: Egress constraints and allowed outbound destinations
Success criteria: p95/p99 latency, throughput, error rate
Security requirements: KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: okay everyone thanks for joining, I'll kick us off. we're here to scope the endpoint isolation pilot for Praesidio, mainly PrivateLink vs peering, residency and the benchmark plan. hope that works?
00:12 Carlos Mendes: yep thanks Maya, quick note, we have to run this pilot inside our us-east-1 tenancy and can't route outside the region — data residency and egress rules are strict.
00:22 Leah Wong: and we need no public internet egress from the subnet where models run, so PrivateLink is attractive but curious on latency/cost tradeoffs.
00:35 Jonah Kim: high level, PrivateLink gives you endpoint isolation and control of egress, peering is simpler but can cross AZs and may require NAT for some flows. performance differences are subtle but cost and operational surface differ.
00:50 Erin Cole: timeline wise, we want a 3-week pilot with the possibility of extending to prod by end of quarter. success criteria are key — we want clear p95/p99 targets and an understanding of unit cost.
01:03 Maya Patel: perfect, let's capture success criteria now. Jonah, what do you recommend for latency SLOs for a gen workload?
01:11 Jonah Kim: for generation workloads at 2k token average request, conservative target p95 under 350ms for model-infer only is aggressive — for us a realistic p95 is 400-750ms depending on model. but we can set pilot targets: p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1200ms, error rate < 0.5%. that's with batching tuned and KV cache warm.
01:32 Ravi Shah: wait can we define "model-infer only" vs total wall time. we have middleware that does enrichment and hits our internal KMS for key retrieval — those hops add latency. we'll need to isolate Redwood's contribution.
01:45 Priya Desai: good call. we'll instrument traces and send token-level latency breakdown so you can attribute. in the pilot we'll run baseline runs with direct calls and then with your KMS hops.
02:00 Leah Wong: on throughput, our peak is roughly 350 QPS for the use case in peak trading windows, but average is 70 QPS. want the pilot to demonstrate both steady-state and burst handling.
02:15 Jonah Kim: ok we'll size the pilot harness to emulate 400 QPS bursts and sustained 75 QPS. we'll do both cold-cache and warm-cache runs to measure delta.
02:27 Carlos Mendes: security-wise we need SOC2 evidence, audit logs, SSO with SAML, RBAC controls and that KMS where keys never leave our VPC. can Redwood integrate with our KMS or do we need to proxy?
02:40 Maya Patel: Redwood Private supports VPC endpoints and can be configured so KMS calls remain inside your network; for hosted we support customer-managed KMS with restricted egress, but we'll confirm exact flows. action: Jonah to map KMS call flow.
02:55 Erin Cole: also, what about model pinning and rollback during the pilot? we need deterministic model versions pinned per route.
03:04 Priya Desai: yes pilot will pin a tuned open model (we suggested open-llama-13b-quant) and also have a fallback smaller model for cost/latency comparisons. we'll include A/B runs.
03:18 Jonah Kim: benchmarks I propose: 1) single-request p95/p99 at 2k tokens; 2) 5-minute sustained 75 QPS; 3) 30s burst to 400 QPS; 4) KV cache warm vs cold; 5) end-to-end with KMS/HSM; and 6) error/failure injection to validate graceful fallback.
03:42 Leah Wong: for egress, audit: any external calls must be to approved endpoints only — we'd like a short list of Redwood-managed IPs or endpoint addresses.
03:52 Maya Patel: we can provide PrivateLink endpoint DNS names and explain NAT usage. for peering you'd see Redwood IP ranges on the peer. we'll supply both ways.
04:05 Carlos Mendes: cost targets — we want to understand unit cost per 1k tokens and expected monthly run rate if adopted. can Redwood provide a rough TCO with dedicated vs hosted?
04:17 Maya Patel: yes, we'll run a cost model for your traffic profile. private/dedicated tends to lower per-token costs at scale but requires commit. we'll include model quantization options in the TCO.
04:30 Ravi Shah: regarding region locking — can you guarantee that model artifacts and logs stay in our region and don't replicate out?
04:38 Jonah Kim: in Private deployment we can guarantee artifacts and logs stay in-region; hosted we can provide region redirection and ensure customer data doesn't cross region boundaries in normal operations — we'll confirm retention backends.
04:52 Erin Cole: what's the expected setup time for PrivateLink pilot? we have internal change windows.
04:57 Priya Desai: usually 2-5 business days for endpoint config, plus 1-2 days for route/table review. if there's co-managed infra we can move faster.
05:10 Carlos Mendes: are there known gotchas with AWS PrivateLink and large streaming responses? we stream tokens to client; need to ensure no chunking issues.
05:20 Jonah Kim: streaming through PrivateLink is fine but we need to ensure connection timeout/window settings are tuned on your ALB/NLB side. we'll share recommended TCP keepalive and idle timeouts.
05:33 Leah Wong: about peering — our security team worries about route propagation and transitive trust. peering would need strict route filters.
05:41 Maya Patel: yes peering requires route controls and careful security reviews. PrivateLink is often preferred for strict egress and zero-public-internet models.
05:52 Erin Cole: success criteria recap? can we list crisp numeric targets to sign off?
06:00 Jonah Kim: propose pilot success criteria: 1) p95 generation latency < 600ms (model-only) and end-to-end p95 < 850ms; 2) withstand 400 QPS burst with error rate < 1% and steady 75 QPS error rate < 0.3%; 3) KV cache warm improves latency by at least 30% vs cold; 4) audit logs delivered to your SIEM with correct fields; 5) no outbound traffic to non-approved endpoints.
06:28 Leah Wong: sounds reasonable, we'll review internally and push back if needed.
06:34 Carlos Mendes: how long will benchmarking take? full set?
06:38 Jonah Kim: plan is 5 working days to run the full bench set, plus 2 days to analyze and deliver results. if we need to iterate on infra tuning add another 2-3 days.
06:50 Priya Desai: we'll provide the test harness and a runbook so your ops can replay tests inside your VPC if you'd like.
07:00 Erin Cole: can you show sample artifacts now — like the test plan or template?
07:04 Maya Patel: we shared a short binder before the call — I'll re-upload the test-plan and endpoint diagram after the meeting.
07:12 Ravi Shah: question on compliance: we need detailed network diagrams and an architecture review as part of our vendor approval. can Redwood provide ATO-friendly docs?
07:22 Maya Patel: yes we have security whitepapers, SOC2 artifacts, and architecture diagrams. I'll attach them.
07:29 Carlos Mendes: any performance differences between quantized models vs full fp16 in PrivateLink?
07:35 Jonah Kim: quantization gives big memory and perf wins typically — 4-bit/8-bit quantized models often reduce latency by 20-40% depending on kernel path. we'll include a small experiment comparing 8-bit vs fp16 on the same instance type.
07:50 Leah Wong: on monitoring, we need token-level cost reporting tied to routes.
07:55 Priya Desai: Redwood Console provides token-level dashboards and per-route costs, and we'll add custom labels for your routes.
08:05 Erin Cole: about fallout — if latency spikes, what are fallback policies?
08:09 Jonah Kim: we support canary and automatic fallback to a smaller model or alternative region/model variant; pilot will test automatic fallback policy and alerting.
08:22 Maya Patel: okay I want to capture explicit next steps — I'll summarize in the follow-up email. Jonah, you'll own the bench plan; Leah will share VPC details; Ravi will send KMS constraints; Maya will send security artifacts.
08:36 Carlos Mendes: small nit — please include a simple cost-per-1M-token estimate for both hosted and dedicated paths in the follow-up.
08:44 Maya Patel: will do. any other questions?
08:48 Erin Cole: not from product.
08:50 Leah Wong: one more, do you support peering with multiple accounts? we have several sub-accounts and may want cross-account peering.
08:57 Priya Desai: yes we can support multi-account PrivateLink/peering setups; we'll document options.
09:05 Jonah Kim: last technical note — we'll include KV cache warmup guidance and recommended batch sizes to hit your latency goals without sacrificing cost.
09:14 Maya Patel: great. thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the deliverables. we'll aim to start bench runs week of 2027-08-30 if you can provide VPC info by 08-25.
09:24 Carlos Mendes: sounds good, thank you.
09:26 [meeting ends with brief cross chatter]
questions: Can Redwood guarantee region-local storage of logs and model artifacts?
What's the expected setup time for PrivateLink endpoint configuration?
How will KMS/HSM calls be handled to avoid egress?
What's the recommended pilot success criteria for p95/p99 and error rate?
